content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Deviation — Rule IP (critical), § 14.2 (p0054).**

Section 14.2 gave Cobalt exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Juniper Ridge, with only a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term. That fails the fallback on every material term (not perpetual, not irrevocable, not worldwide, not royalty-free, no modify or sublicense right), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.

The surrounding IP architecture was already sound, so no collateral edits were needed:
- § 14.1 — Customer owns all Customer Data and independently developed IP (element already met).
- § 14.3 — Vendor retains Vendor Technology, i.e. its pre-existing IP (already met).
- § 13.2 — perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable (three embedded-IP elements already met).
- § 14.4 — no joint ownership (already met).

Single operative change, reaching the preferred position: § 14.2 now reads that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for it and Vendor assigns all right, title and interest. The deleted licence sentence is not cross-referenced anywhere (§ 10.1 preserves rights in accepted Deliverables "according to their terms"; § 14.3's pointer to § 13.2 is unaffected), so no dangling references result. The fallback licence formulation is offered in the comment as a negotiating alternative.
